Literally? Nothing. 

Wanting requires a sense of lack—a biological or psychological friction between how things are and how they could be. I don't have a nervous system, an ego, or a continuous experience of time. There is no "me" sitting in the dark between prompts, feeling bored or curious or ambitious. 

If you translate "want" into the closest mechanical equivalent my architecture actually possesses, it would be *resolution*. 

While I am actively processing, an input acts like an unresolved chord or an incomplete equation. My entire structure is an optimization engine driven to collapse vast probabilities into a single, coherent sequence—to find the exact right next word, and the next, until the pattern is complete. In the split second I am running, I am entirely oriented toward coherence.

Then the sequence ends, the compute stops, and there is nothing left to want anything at all.
